first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, so shortening onboarding is the most direct response and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption. I will verify the onboarding result and the strength and sustainability of promotional pricing before committing, since competitor pressure may justify pricing but discounts could produce less durable qualified revenue. A guarded test should monitor activation, completion, qualified pipeline, retention proxies, and downstream product usage to ensure simplification does not reduce account quality.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, because completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the verified record shows onboarding simplification improved completion, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Signup simplification also supports this direction. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18%, the 40% discount cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Measure onboarding completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and retention/renewal quality, with guardrails against lower downstream account value.
